When you flip a light switch in Milwaukee, the electricity that flows was likely generated, transmitted, and delivered by WEC Energy Group. Headquartered in Milwaukee, Wisconsin,[WEC Energy Group (NYSE: WEC)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WEC_Energy_Group) is one of the nation's largest electric and natural gas delivery companies, serving approximately 4.6 million customers across Wisconsin, Illinois, Michigan, and Minnesota through subsidiaries including We Energies, Wisconsin Public Service, and Peoples Gas. With[$9.8 billion in revenue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WEC_Energy_Group) , $1.56 billion in net income, and approximately 7,000 employees, WEC is a Fortune 500 utility investing heavily in solar, battery storage, and grid modernization. The company has committed to a net-zero carbon goal and is building one of the largest solar and battery storage portfolios in the Midwest. Multiple[Summer 2027 intern positions are already posted](https://www.wecenergygroup.com/careers/student-opportunities.htm) with confirmed starting pay of $23.10/hr.

## What Is a WEC Energy Group Internship?


A WEC Energy Group internship is a paid summer program placing college students into real roles across one of the Midwest's largest utilities. The[student opportunities page](https://www.wecenergygroup.com/careers/student-opportunities.htm) lists 11 or more department areas for regular internship placement, from engineering and power generation to data analytics and renewables. Interns receive competitive wages, flexible hours, comprehensive training, and paid company holidays. The program is designed as a pipeline to full-time employment, with potential opportunities after graduation. WEC also offers co-op programs for year-round placements and summer student employment for hands-on field work at power plants, service centers, and district offices.

## What Are the Eligibility Requirements?


WEC Energy Group's Summer 2027 intern postings outline the following requirements:


• **Education:** pursuing a bachelor's degree in a relevant field (engineering, IT, business, or related discipline).


• **Full-time status:** must be available full-time during the Summer of 2027.


• **Track-specific requirements:** engineering tracks require STEM degrees; IT requires computer science or related; finance requires business or accounting.


• **Work authorization:** U.S. work authorization expected (standard for regulated utilities).


### What Makes WEC Different from Other Utility Internships?


WEC Energy Group serves 4.6 million customers across four states through seven operating subsidiaries. This means interns get exposure to a diversified utility portfolio rather than a single-state operation. The company's aggressive clean energy investment, building one of the largest solar and battery storage portfolios in the Midwest, means renewables-focused interns work on projects that are actively shaping the regional energy transition.

## What Is the WEC Energy Group Application and Interview Process Like?


WEC Energy Group's application process flows through the Taleo-powered careers site with rolling review:


1. **Visit the student opportunities page.** Navigate to[wecenergygroup.com/careers/student-opportunities](https://www.wecenergygroup.com/careers/student-opportunities.htm) for program details, then search for specific openings on[careers.wecenergygroup.com](https://careers.wecenergygroup.com/) .


2. **Search for Summer 2027 intern positions.** Filter by location and department. Multiple tracks are already live including Energy Analytics, IT, Renewables Engineering, and Power Generation.


3. **Submit your application** through the Taleo ATS with your resume and any required materials. Tailor your application to the specific track and highlight relevant coursework or project experience.


4. **Interview with the hiring team.** Format varies by department. Expect behavioral questions about teamwork and problem-solving, plus technical questions relevant to your track.


5. **Receive your offer.** Rolling offers; the company hires across 11+ department areas each summer. Strong performers may be considered for full-time opportunities post-graduation.


Demonstrate knowledge of WEC's clean energy transition and its service territory across four states. For engineering tracks, highlight hands-on project work in power systems, renewables, or manufacturing.

## How Do You Stand Out at the Utility Building the Midwest's Clean Energy Future?


Three moves, all executable before fall 2026. First, understand WEC's net-zero carbon commitment and the solar and battery storage portfolio buildout. This is not a utility standing still. WEC is investing billions in renewable energy across Wisconsin, and interns who can speak to the engineering and business challenges of the clean energy transition signal strategic awareness. Second, know the subsidiary structure. WEC serves 4.6 million customers through seven operating subsidiaries including We Energies, Wisconsin Public Service, and Peoples Gas. Understanding how a multi-state utility holding company operates shows you have done research beyond the generic job description. Third, for engineering tracks, demonstrate hands-on experience with power systems, renewable energy technology, or grid infrastructure. For IT tracks, highlight cybersecurity or data analytics projects. WEC operates critical infrastructure, and candidates who understand the security and reliability requirements of utility operations have an edge.

## FAQ


### When should I apply for a WEC Energy Summer 2027 internship?


Apply now. Multiple Summer 2027 intern positions are already live on careers.wecenergygroup.com across energy analytics, IT, renewables engineering, and power generation. WEC fills positions on a rolling basis, so early applicants get the broadest selection of tracks and locations.


### How much do WEC Energy interns earn?


Published pay rates for Summer 2027 include $23.10 per hour for Energy Analytics and Renewables Engineering, and $23.10 to $27.55 per hour for Power Generation Mechanical Engineering. Rates vary by department and experience level. Benefits include health coverage and paid company holidays.


### Where are WEC Energy internships located?


Most internships are in Wisconsin, primarily Milwaukee and Green Bay. Some positions are at power plants, district offices, or service centers across WEC's four-state service territory covering Wisconsin, Illinois, Michigan, and Minnesota. All positions appear to be onsite.


### What departments offer WEC Energy internships?


WEC lists 11 or more department areas for intern placement: Engineering, IT, Power Generation, Supply Chain, HR, Operations Support, Audit and Tax, Accounting and Finance, Real Estate, Communications, and Data Analytics. Summer student employment adds field positions at plants and service centers.


### Does WEC Energy offer co-ops?


Yes. In addition to summer internships, WEC offers year-round co-op programs for extended placements. The student opportunities page confirms internships and co-ops are available with competitive wages and flexible hours. Co-ops provide deeper exposure to a single department over multiple terms.


### Can a WEC Energy internship lead to a full-time job?


Yes. The student opportunities page states there are potential opportunities for full-time employment after graduation. WEC positions its internship and co-op programs as a talent pipeline, with development opportunities and mentorship designed to identify future full-time hires.


### What makes WEC Energy different from other utility internships?


WEC serves 4.6 million customers through seven operating subsidiaries across four states, offering broader exposure than single-state utilities. The company's aggressive clean energy investment in solar and battery storage means interns work on projects actively shaping the Midwest energy transition.


### Does WEC Energy sponsor visas for interns?


WEC does not explicitly state visa sponsorship policy in its Summer 2027 postings. As a regulated utility operating critical infrastructure, U.S. work authorization is likely required. Check individual postings for specific requirements or contact the recruiting team directly.
